transcript: Three things you can do when your mind will not stop thinking about something you cannot control. That loop where your brain keeps walking back to the same thought again and again, even though you know thinking about it more, will not change anything. Still, the mind returns. Because the brain sees uncertainty as danger, it keeps the file open because it believes something still needs to be solved. But some things cannot be solved by thinking harder. They must be placed down. First, written containment. Take a paper and write the problem in one sentence, then make two columns. What I can control, what I cannot control. This is not journaling. This is giving the mind a place to put the thought. When you write it down, the mind finally sees what belongs to you and what does not. Second, a worry window. Tell your mind, I will think about this later. Set a time. When the thought comes back, gently send it there. This tells the brain it does not need to carry the thought all day. Third, a body reset before bed. Stand up. Shake your hands for 30 seconds. Take five deep sighs. Then say out loud, I have done what I can with this today. Not because everything is finished, but because your nervous system needs a signal of completion. Some things cannot be solved tonight, but they do not need to be carried all night. And if your mind has been heavy for too long, start the 30-day healing journey. Go to the link in my profile to begin.
